text.text_excerpt: Love this hip coffee spot. The seating area is mostly outside and dotted with original furniture pieces that look like they were found at a variety of yard sales. It's awesome. The iced coffee was strong and delicious. I also opted for the yogurt and granola to shoot for a healthier choice, but that yogurt definitely tasted like full fat. I'm not complaining -- it was delicious. I just won't be focusing on my diet here. I'll DEFINITELY be returning to get some work done. Also thank god for its early hours!! I start work early, so there aren't always a ton of places open. This one opens at 6.

When I was driving past their new location on St. Claude I could hardly believe it! "Fair Grinds moved from the Fairgrounds to St. Claude?!" No, even better, it's their new, second location. And I love it. Another coffee option that's within walking distance. The new location has plenty of outdoor seating in the alleyway leading up to the shop, which is smallish, but there's a fair amount of seating and outlets inside, too. As you may or may not know, Fair Grinds has a mission behind their coffee (fair trade, locally sourced baked goods - didn't see any vegan treats, but hopefully they'll add some). The iced coffee is cold drip and that's just what I needed on a recent steamy Saturday. Oh...

I walk past Fairgrinds at least once a week and always want to go in. How do the make that alleyway so inviting! They could teach Cellar Door a thing or two. Today I had time and stress that only a caramel iced coffee could soothe so, I stopped in. The barista was attentive but not pushy as I perused the menu and refrigerator full of goodies. The drink was delicious and the sandwich yummy. What most suprised me, because I spend too much time in starbucks, was how reasonable the prices were. Normally I expect an upcharge for do-gooder organizations like this one but they are pretty on par with the rest of the market in this part of town. Good for you and for me too! No suggestions for impr...
